newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures end flat in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures end flat in Tokyo.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended Monday's day session flat, with market participants continuing to eye the Japanese government bond (JGB) futures market for cues, traders said.
The June contract settled at 99.08, unchanged from Friday, after trading between 99.06 and 99.12.
Turnover of the June contract was 57,161 contracts.

"Euroyen futures showed no big movement today as they were lacking a sense of direction after the recent sharp fall. The June contract was only moving in tandem with the JGB futures market," said a trader at a Japanese brokerage house.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) released Japan's wholesale price index (WPI) for October this morning, but the market's reaction was muted as the data had been expected to confirm a stable price condition, traders said.
The domestic WPI, a key component of overall WPI, was down 0.2 percent from September and down 0.7 percent from a year earlier.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.48 percent, up from 0.45 percent on Friday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 800 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
A rise in the overnight rate today had been widely anticipated, as its slip on Friday was largely due to weekend factors, traders said.
The overnight rate was underpinned by demand for funds ahead of the end of the current reserve maintenance period on Friday, traders said.
The key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Friday.
About 20 billion yen worth of two-month CDs was issued at 0.50 percent, and about 65 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.49 percent. Both rates were unchanged from Friday.
